params.body:
This replaces PR #309, rebased on `main` after the duplicate-chassis merge (#308); because #308 already took `X-87`, the three Car-Pass findings were renumbered to `X-88`, `X-89` and `X-90`, and both generated files were regenerated from scratch rather than hand-merged.

## Why the click looked dead

`App\Livewire\OwnStockList::requestCarpass()` called `CarpassController::carpassRequest()` and
threw the return value away:

```php
try {
    app(CarpassController::class)->carpassRequest((int) $id);
} catch (\Throwable $e) {
    report($e);
}
```

So a click on "Car-Pass aanvragen" in the own-stock list was indistinguishable from doing
nothing. A success only became visible after a manual refresh; a refusal never became visible at
all. On staging the request in fact *does* leave for the Car-Pass beta environment and comes back
with a real message — the screen simply stayed silent.

## Which signal says "success"

Not `status`. `carpassRequest()` has return paths with `'status' => 'success'` **and**
`'error' => 1` (the sealed environment, the unsafe-endpoint guard, an authentication error), and
paths with `'status' => 'error'` and `'error' => 1` (an issue reported by Car-Pass). The only
path that sets `carpass_init` and `carpass_id` returns `'error' => 0`. **`error` is the signal:
0 is success, anything else is not.** A naive `status === 'success'` check would paint a failure
green, so both shapes are pinned in a test.

## What the dealer now sees

| Outcome | On screen |
|---|---|
| Success (`error` 0) | Green notify: "Car-Pass aangevraagd en aan de wagen gekoppeld." The row re-renders, so the chip becomes the Car-Pass link. |
| Demo dealer | The flag is flipped as before, and the same green notify. Demo and a real dealer behave identically on screen. |
| Refusal (`error` 1, action `correction` or none) | Red notify carrying Car-Pass's own message ("De kilometerstand ligt lager dan …"), never a generic "er ging iets mis". |
| Unknown chassis number (issue 131, action `correction_or_confirm`) | A `ui.dialog` with Car-Pass's message and two named choices: **Chassisnummer bevestigen** (re-runs the flow with `action=confirm`) or **Chassisnummer aanpassen** (goes to the vehicle sheet). Cancel does nothing. |
| Thrown exception | `report($e)` as before, **plus** a red notify with the exception message — unless that message looks like it carries a credential (a password/token/secret word, a URL with userinfo) or is too long to be a sentence, in which case the neutral Car-Pass wording is shown and the full error stays in the log. |

The wording deliberately says a Car-Pass was created and linked, not that a history document is
ready: after a confirmed unknown chassis number `handleVhrResult()` yields a `publicUrl` without
a document. One sentence that is true for both outcomes.

The unknown-chassis case was a dead end before this PR: a second identical request answers
exactly the same, so a car Car-Pass does not know (an import, an oldtimer, a car that never drove
in Belgium) could never get a Car-Pass from this screen. The whole chain (observation → status →
issue 131 → confirm → VHR) is proven end to end on staging.

All of it rides the channel that already existed: `$this->dispatch('flash', …)`, which
`resources/views/components/ui/notify.blade.php` listens for. That listener gained an optional
`tone`, so a failure can be red without a second mechanism. `ui.confirm` / `ui.dialog` /
`ui.notify` only; no library, no second toast.

## The `request()` keys

`carpassRequest()` reads `request()->get('chassis')`, `->get('mileage')`, `->get('action')` and
`->get('issueId')`. Findings:

* **Nothing leaks in.** A Livewire update is a POST to `/livewire/update` — a path with no route
  parameters — whose JSON body carries only `_token` and `components` at the top level. The
  method params live inside `components[].calls[].params`. `request()->get()` reads route
  attributes, then query, then input, so none of the four keys can be present, and no middleware
  in this app merges anything into the request. There was no defect to fix here.
* **But the absence was itself the dead end.** Because `action` is always empty in a Livewire
  call, the flow could never ask for anything but an observation, and so could never get past
  issue 131.
* **Chosen fix:** `carpassRequest($id, $by_cron = false, ?string $action = null)` — an explicit
  third argument, honoured by `resolveCarpassAction()` before it falls back to the request keys.
  The classic HTTP route is untouched. No `request()->merge()`: a caller faking a payload for
  another caller's reading is exactly how this kind of thing goes wrong later.
* Confirming is its own Livewire method (`confirmCarpassChassis`), not an `action` parameter on
  `requestCarpass`. Public Livewire methods are callable from the browser, and the browser should
  not name the call that leaves for Car-Pass.

The refusal payload also carries `action` and `issueId`, which steer what a next attempt would
do. We do not act on them beyond the 131 case; they go to `Log::warning` with the vehicle id, so
a developer can see them without turning the step log on. They never appear in the notify text.

## The dead classic branch

`resources/views/ownstock/_wagen_rij.blade.php:145` rendered, for `$lw === false`, an
`<a class="… carpass_init_switch">` with `data-chassis` / `data-milage` / `data-id`. No
JavaScript in the repo binds `carpass_init_switch` any more — the only reference left was CSS.
The single include of this partial passes `lw => true`, so nothing rendered it, but anything that
ever did would have shown a button that silently does nothing. **Removed**, together with its two
orphan rules in `resources/css/refresh.css`. The non-Livewire path now falls through to the
honest passive "Geen Car-Pass" chip.

## Second defect, found while diagnosing: the flow log was silent on every server

`CarpassController::shouldLogCarpassFlowSteps()` returned false when
`vendor/barryvdh/laravel-debugbar` was absent. A deploy installs with `--no-dev`, so that
directory exists on no server at all, and `grep 'Car-Pass flow' storage/logs/laravel.log` on
staging returned nothing while a request was in fact going out. A dev dependency is not a
switch. Replaced by `CARPASS_FLOW_LOG` (`config/services.php`, documented in `.env.example`):
unset means off in production and on everywhere else. The log carries the call, the requestGuid,
the status and the issue — never a credential.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/CarpassRequestFeedbackTest.php`, nine cases: demo success, a refusal carrying
Car-Pass's wording, the mixed `status=success` + `error=1` shape, a processed report, a thrown
exception, an exception whose text carries a credential, the unknown-chassis choice, the confirm
action reaching the controller, and a plain request asking for an observation. Plus the existing
guard on a foreign vehicle. The controller is replaced in the container by a stand-in, so no
outbound call is made and the Outbound seal is never consulted.

Rules: `R S3-2.15` (what the platform shows after a request), `R S3-2.16` (the flow log and its
switch) and `R S3-2.17` (the unknown-chassis choice) added to
`docs/bedrijfsregels/13-s3-car-pass.md`; `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html`
regenerated. Findings `X-88` (silent click), `X-89` (flow log gated on a dev dependency) and
`X-90` (unknown chassis number was a dead end) recorded in `90-x-bevindingen.md`.

Verified locally: `OwnStockList|Carpass|CarPass|RulesCoverage|StylesheetSyntax|BuildContract|SmokeTest`
— 181 tests, 962 assertions, green.
